audioNote.markdown:
Welcome to Sessionboard! In this video, we will walk you through the steps to create an evaluation plan for session review. 

Evaluation Plans are for gathering feedback for your submitted sessions by outside evaluators, such as committees, using a rating scale.

steps.title: Configuration

audioNote.markdown:
Additionally, there are 4 settings you can configure.

'Set Plan as Open'. If enabled, you can set a due date. If the plan remains closed, you can open the plan at a later date. Until then, plans are "view-only" to evaluators. 

'Enable Anonymized Review'. The first & last names of session speakers are removed from submission details.

'Enable Weekly Reminders'. Have an automated email sent to evaluators every Monday when there are sessions to review in their plan.

'Include Uploaded Files'. Toggle this option on if you want evaluators to view and access any files uploaded to sessions. To learn more about this feature, watch our Session Files Training Video.

steps.title: Select Evaluators

audioNote.markdown:
On page four, apply filters to determine which sessions appear in the plan. You can create multiple plans with different filters to organize sessions for review, such as track, tags, format, level, language, or status. 

For example, create one plan for each track and assign evaluators to a plan based on their area of expertise.

audioNote.markdown:
On the final page, choose a rating icon for your plan. There are four options: star and heart icons can be set up to 20, while face and number icons have a maximum of 5.

steps.title: Grading Options

audioNote.markdown: Rubrics allow evaluators to score submissions based on specific criteria you define. Each criterion is weighted and contributes to an overall average score. Use the Add Criteria button to include more, or customize the existing options. Adjust the sliding scale to ensure all criteria add up to 100%.

steps.title: Rubric

audioNote.markdown:
Lastly, you can set an evaluation limit that tells your evaluators how many times the evaluation team should review each submission. The number of evaluations per session is tied to the number of evaluators assigned to the plan. For example, If four evaluators are assigned to the plan, each submission can be reviewed a maximum of four times. 

Once you are complete, click the Add Plan button to create your evaluation plan.
